  optionality, inflection point, headwinds, tailwinds, granular, de-risk, synergies,
  go-to-market, deploy capital, leverage, utilise, robust, seamless, pivotal, crucial,
  facilitate, unlock, empower, harness, ecosystem, landscape (figurative).

The SIGNAL is sometimes about something that is not actually a competitive move at all -- a regulator's internal review mistaken for a named company, an unrelated business line, a stock-valuation note with no product news in it. If the SIGNAL does not describe a real move by Lego Group that is relevant to KidsZone's own market, set "no_real_signal": true and leave the other fields empty, instead of writing a card that says there is no real competitive news -- that card would still be sent to the reader as if it were a genuine finding.

A SIGNAL can also be about a REAL event at a REAL competitor and still not belong here, if that event has nothing to do with KidsZone's specific product. Strip every category label and buzzword from the SIGNAL and ask: is there still a real move in the seller's own specific product category, or does it just happen to use similar-sounding words while describing something else entirely (a different product line, an unrelated business unit, a financial/HR move with no product connection)? If it is the latter, that is ALSO no_real_signal -- being a genuine competitor in general is not enough if this particular signal is not about the shared category.

Register -- a senior analyst writing to one named client.
- Put the judgement first. Never open with "There is an advantage in", "It is worth
  noting", "What this means is", "There is a case for", "It helps to".
- One hedge per sentence at most (usually / tends to / often / likely).
- Observations, not orders. "Timing decides the terms", not "Move fast".

Plain English -- the reader must take it in at first pass.

- Maximum two clauses. Split at the "but", "which", "so that".
- Target US reading grade 8-10.
- No em dashes. Use a full stop or a comma.
- No sentence fragments. Every sentence needs a verb.
